t.1.121.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Bhīṣma, seeking something exceptional and wishing for the proper training of his grandsons, inquired after teachers skilled in arrows and weapons and esteemed for their valor.
t.1.121.3: Long ago the great seer Bharadvāja, while moving about at Havirdhāna, beheld with his own eyes the Apsaras Ghṛtācī, who had just bathed.
t.1.121.2: No one of little intelligence, no one who is not greatly distinguished, nor likewise one unversed in the various weapons, no one lacking godlike strength could train the mighty Kurus in weaponry.
t.1.121.5: In that pitcher of the wise one, Droṇa came into being; he studied the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas in their entirety.
t.1.121.6: The mighty Bharadvāja, best among the upholders of dharma, imparted the fiery weapon of Agni to the illustrious Agniveśya.
t.1.121.4: A gust of wind that had risen pulled away her garment. Then his seed spilled, and the seer laid it down; that seed was Droṇa.
t.1.121.8: And there was a king named Pṛṣata, a friend of Bharadvāja; to him too a son named Drupada was born at that time.
t.1.121.9: Going constantly to the hermitage, that son of Pṛṣata, a bull among kṣatriyas, played together with Droṇa and also pursued his studies.
t.1.121.7: Then, O best of the Bharatas, that sage born of Agniṣṭut imparted to Bhāradvāja that great fiery weapon.
t.1.121.10: Then, when Pṛṣata had passed away, that mighty-armed Drupada became king, lord of men among the northern Pāñcālas.
t.1.121.11: Then the blessed Bharadvāja too ascended to heaven. Thereafter the greatly renowned Droṇa, his mind set on it by his father's injunction and out of longing for a son, took Kṛpī, the daughter of Śaradvat, as his wife.
t.1.121.12: Gautamī, ever devoted to the fire-offering, to dharma and to self-restraint, obtained a son, Aśvatthāman.
t.1.121.14: Since the might of this one, as he cried out like a horse, went forth to all the quarters, this boy shall therefore be known by the name Aśvatthāman.
t.1.121.13: As soon as he was born, he neighed just like the horse Uccaiḥśravas. Hearing that, an invisible being stationed in the sky spoke.
t.1.121.15: Then Bhāradvāja became exceedingly pleased with that son, and, dwelling there, the wise one became wholly devoted to the science of archery.
t.1.121.16: Then, O king, he heard that the great-souled Jāmadagnya, scorcher of foes, wished to give away all his wealth to the brāhmaṇas.
t.1.121.17: Then Bhāradvāja spoke to Rāma, who had set out for the forest: "Know me to be Droṇa, a bull among the twice-born, who has come here desiring wealth."
t.1.121.18: Whatever gold I had, and whatever other wealth there was, all of it I have given away to the brāhmaṇas, O you whose wealth is austerity.
t.1.121.19: Likewise, this goddess Earth, bounded by the ocean, with her towns and garlanded with cities, has been given by me in her entirety to Kaśyapa.
t.1.121.21: Droṇa said: O Bhārgava, you ought to give me all the weapons in their entirety, together with the means of withdrawing them, along with the secrets of their use, leaving nothing out.
t.1.121.20: Only this body, along with my precious divine missiles and weapons of many kinds, has been left by me today. Choose: what shall I give you, Droṇa? Tell me that quickly.
t.1.121.23: Having received all of that, the best of the twice-born, now accomplished in weapons, went in great delight to Drupada, his dear friend.
t.1.121.22: Saying, “So be it,” the Bhārgava then gave him the weapons, and the entire science of archery as well, together with its secrets and vows.
